children.translated_text: <s>Aurva</s> said:
When <s>Bhūteśa</s> had spoken thus, then <s>Vetāla</s> and <s>Bhairava</s>,
their eyes expanded with joy, spoke to <s>Vyomakeśa</s>.
<s>Vetāla</s> and <s>Bhairava</s> said:

children.text: pārvatyā na hi jānīvo dhyānaṃ mantraṃ vidhiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: We do not know the meditation, the mantra, or the procedure for <s>Pārvatī</s>.
How shall we worship her, Blessed Lord? Let it be properly explained.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: mahāmāyāvidhiṃ mantraṃ kalpaṃ ca bhavatoḥ sutau
children.translated_text: O two sons, I shall teach you both the procedure, the mantra, and the ritual manual of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>,
in truth, by which everything will be accomplished.
<s>Aurva</s> said:

children.text: ityuktvā sa mahāmāyādhyānaṃ mantraṃ vidhiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Giriśa</s> then explained the meditation, mantra, and procedure of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>,
properly to the two of them, O best of kings.
Afterwards that <s>Bhairava</s>, in eighteen chapters,
composed the determining procedure and ritual manual in the <s>Śivāmṛta</s>.
<s>Sagara</s> said:
What sort of mantra did <s>Śambhu</s> formerly teach to those two,
by worshipping <s>Mahāmāyā</s> with which they attained the rank of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>?
I wish to hear it, together with its ritual procedure, its secret, and its auxiliaries,
which that <s>Bhairava</s> composed in the eighteen chapters.
<s>Aurva</s> said:

children.text: bahutvād vadituṃ tasya cireṇaiva tu śakyate
children.translated_text: Because of its great extent, it can be told only over a long time.
Therefore, extracting at once what was spoken by <s>Mahādeva</s>,
I shall tell the truth in brief. Listen to it, O best of kings.
When <s>Vetāla</s> and <s>Bhairava</s> were asking about the mantra of <s>Pārvatī</s>,
then <s>Mahādeva</s> said, "Listen, you two who know mantra-procedure."
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: śṛṇu mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyād guhyatamaṃ param
children.translated_text: Listen. I shall teach the supreme mantra, the most secret of secrets,
the eight-syllabled great festival-mantra of <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> <s>Mahāmāyā</s>.
For this holy <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the seer and <s>Śambhu</s> is the deity.
The meter is <s>anuṣṭubh</s>; its application is for the accomplishment of all aims.
It begins with the syllable ending in ha, then the one ending in ra, and likewise those ending in na and ṇa;
then the eleventh, the eighth, the sixth, and the one ending in kha, preceded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
With these eight syllables the mantra, shining like a red leaf,

children.text: oṃkāraṃ pūrvataḥ kṛtvā japyaṃ sarvaistu sādhakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be recited by all practitioners, placing the syllable oṃ before it.
This secret great mantra is known as the <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> mantra.
Since the mantra is embodied, its limb is therefore proclaimed.
This is declared to be the seed from the upward face of <s>Mahādeva</s>.
The syllable-seed is oṃ, and the letter ya is called the power.

children.text: sabījaṃ kathitaṃ mantraṃ kalpaṃ ca śṛṇu bhairava
children.translated_text: The mantra with its seed has been told. Now hear the ritual procedure, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
At a tīrtha, in a river, in a divine pool, in a pit, spring, or the like,
or in water that belongs to another or does not belong to another, one should first perform bathing.
Having sipped water and attained purity, having taken possession of a seat,
one should face north and then cleanse the sacred ground.

children.text: kareṇānena mantreṇa yūṃ saḥ kṣityā iti svayam ||
children.translated_text: With the hand, by this mantra, "yūṃ saḥ kṣityā," one should do it oneself.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ sa iti mantreṇa āśāpūraṇakena ca
children.translated_text: With the mantra "oṃ hrīṃ sa" and with the wish-fulfilling formula,
one should sprinkle the place with water for the driving away of beings.

children.text: tataḥ savyena hastena gṛhītvā sthaṇḍilaṃ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Then, being pure, taking the sacred ground with the left hand,

children.text: mantraṃ likhet suvarṇena yājñikena kuśena vā ||
children.translated_text: one should write the mantra with gold or with sacrificial kuśa grass.

children.text: oṃ vaiṣṇavyai nama iti mantrarājamathāpi vā
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the king of mantras, "oṃ vaiṣṇavyai namaḥ," may be used.
Then one should make three circles with that same even line.

children.text: nityāsu na hi pūjāsu rajobhirmaṇḍalaṃ likhet
children.translated_text: In daily worships one should not draw the mandala with colored powders.
One should employ that in rites of preliminary practice and in rites performed for a desired object.
The first line should be in the north, and after that in the west;

children.text: dakṣiṇe tu tataḥ paścāt pūrvabhāge tu śeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then in the south, and afterwards the remaining one in the eastern quarter.

children.text: varṇānāṃ ca saha dvārair evameva kramo bhavet
children.translated_text: The same sequence should apply for the letters together with the gates.

children.text: oṃ hīṃ śrīṃ sa iti mantreṇa maṇḍalaṃ pūjayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should worship the mandala with the mantra "oṃ hīṃ śrīṃ sa."

children.text: hastena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā kuryād digbandhanaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having made the mandala with the hand, one should then perform the binding of the directions,
in due order, with the previously stated mantra for binding the quarters.
Here, with the formula ending in phaṭ, one should bind it also oneself, with the hand alone.
One circle of barley grains should be one finger-breadth, and by eight such measures,
with hands not joined lengthwise, twenty-four finger-breadths are made.
With a hand of that measure, its mandala is to be one hand in size.
The lotus should be a span in measure, and its pericarp half of that.
One should arrange the petals long and touching one another.
They should not be in deficient or excessive portions, and they should be surrounded outside.

children.text: madhyabhāge nyased dvāraṃ na nyūne nādhike tathā
children.translated_text: In the middle part one should place the gate, neither deficient nor excessive.
One should visualize that well-constructed mandala as red in color.
Whoever otherwise makes her fierce mandala lacking in its marks and proportions

children.text: phalaṃ na cāpnoti na kāmamiṣṭaṃ tasmād idaṃ maṇḍalamatra lekhyam ||
children.translated_text: does not obtain the fruit or the desired aim; therefore this mandala is to be drawn here.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: tato laṃ iti mantreṇa arghapātrasya maṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Then, with the mantra "laṃ," one should make the mandala of the arghya vessel
quickly as a quadrangle, without gate or lotus.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ itimantreṇa arghapātraṃ tu maṇḍale
children.translated_text: With the mantra "oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ," one should first place the arghya vessel on the mandala there,
after worshipping it, and it becomes kindled.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ iti mantreṇa gandhapuṣpe tathā jalam
children.translated_text: With the mantra "oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ," one should put sandal, flowers, and also water

children.text: arghapātre kṣipet tatra maṇḍalaṃ vinyaset tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: there into the arghya vessel, and then one should set down the mandala.
Making the mandala as before, one should then fill the arghya vessel with water
to three parts, and should throw a flower into it.

children.text: tato hrīṃ iti mantreṇa āsanaṃ pūjayetsvakam
children.translated_text: Then, with the mantra "hrīṃ," one should worship one's own seat.

children.text: tataḥ kṣauṃ iti mantreṇa ātmānaṃ pūjayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the mantra "kṣauṃ," the wise man should worship himself.

children.text: gandhaiḥ puṣpaiḥ śirodeśe tataḥ pūjāṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: Then he should perform the worship at the region of the head with fragrances and flowers.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ sa iti mantreṇa puṣpaṃ hastatalasthitam ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra 'oṃ hrīṃ sa,' the flower placed in the palm of the hand should be used.
Having wiped it with the left hand, and having smelled it with the left hand,
the learned man should place it in the northeast with the preceding mantra.

children.text: raktaṃ puṣpaṃ gṛhītvā tu karābhyāṃ pāṇikacchapam
children.translated_text: Taking a red flower with both hands, having bound the pāṇikacchapa hand-formation,
he should thereafter perform burning, flooding, and the other rites.
He should join the little finger of the right hand to the forefinger of the left hand,
and likewise the left thumb to the right forefinger.
Keeping the right thumb raised, he should join the middle and other fingers of the left hand

children.text: aṅgulīr yojayet pṛṣṭhe dakṣiṇasya karasya ca ||
children.translated_text: on the back of the right hand.
With the pitṛtīrtha of the left hand, the middle and ring fingers likewise

children.text: adhomukhe tu te kuryād dakṣiṇasya karasya ca ||
children.translated_text: should be made face downward on the right hand.
From the right hand he should make a back like the back of a tortoise.
Thus bound, the pāṇikacchapa grants every accomplishment.
The wise man should hold it close to his heart, close both eyes,
make body, head, and neck even, and keep his mind steady.
He should begin meditation on the Goddess, preceded by burning and flooding.

children.text: agniṃ vāyau vinikṣipya vāyuṃ toye jalaṃ hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: He should cast fire into wind, wind into water, and water into the heart.
Having set the heart in stillness, he should place his own sound in space.

children.text: ūṃ hūṃ phaḍiti mantreṇa bhittvā randhraṃ tu mastake ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra 'ūṃ hūṃ phaṭ,' he should pierce the aperture in the head.
Then he should establish the individual life, together with sound, in space.
With the seed-syllables of wind, fire, Yama, Śakra, and Varuṇa,
and with these, furnished with half-moons and bindus, turned to the supreme station,
drying, burning, sweeping away, and the supreme drinking of nectar
are to be performed in order, by thought alone, for purification.
Then, with the Goddess's seed-syllable, he should bring there a minute form shaped like gold,

children.text: tatrāsādya dvidhā kuryāt uṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ iti mantrakāḥ
children.translated_text: and divide it in two; the mantra-syllables are 'uṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ.'

children.text: tadūrdhvabhāgeṣu hṛllokaṃ svargaṃ ca khaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: In its upper parts he should produce the heart-world, heaven, and space,
and with the remaining part the earth in the waters of the underworld.
There he should contemplate all things, and the earth with its seven islands.
Within those he should contemplate the oceans and the golden island.
In the middle of that is a jeweled couch set within a jeweled pavilion.
It is auspicious, always served by streams of water from the heavenly Gaṅgā.
On that couch he should contemplate a red lotus, gracious and identical with Sadāśiva.
It is marked with gold and has its stalk in the seven underworlds,
with a golden mountain as its pericarp, touching as far as Brahmā's world.
There, with one-pointed mind, he should meditate on <s>Mahāmāyā</s> standing there.
She is like a red lotus, with loosened hair hanging from her head,
mounted on moving gold, and shining with radiant earrings.
She wears a double crown endowed with gold and jewels.
She is beautifully adorned with three eyes, white, black, and red.
Her cheeks are as splendid as the twilight moon, and her eyes are restless.
Her teeth are like flawless pomegranate seeds, and she shines with beautiful brows joined in grace.
Her lips are like bandhūka flowers, and her nose has the lustre of śirīṣa.
She has a conch-like neck, large eyes, and a radiance like ten million suns.
She is four-armed, unclothed, with full and high breasts.
In her upper right hand she bears a sword, and in the other a siddha-thread,
while with her left hands she grants fearlessness and boons.
She has a deep navel, a slender waist, and a charming form.
Her thighs bend like serpent nooses, her ankles are hidden, and her heels are beautiful.
She is conceived as seated in the bound cross-legged posture and adorned with the heroic seat.
With her body she stands properly leaning upon a jeweled pillar.
Again and again she utters the words, 'What do you desire?'
looking at the five-faced one standing before her, with his excellent vehicle.
With strings of pearls, gold, jeweled necklaces, bracelets, and the like,
she shines with every host of ornaments, her face smiling.
She is like ten million suns in brilliance and endowed with every auspicious mark.
She is possessed of fresh youth and beautiful in every limb.
Having meditated on <s>Ambikā</s> in this form, with 'namaḥ phaṭ' at the head,

children.text: svakīye prathamaṃ dadyāt so'hameva vicintya ca ||
children.translated_text: he should first place it on his own head, thinking, 'I myself am she.'
Then he should perform aṅganyāsa and karanyāsa in order.
With these mantras, together with the vowels, and with the sequences su, mī, sū, and mai,

children.text: oṃ kṣauṃ caite sapraṇavāṃ raktavarṇāṃ manoharām
children.translated_text: and with 'oṃ kṣauṃ,' these, preceded by praṇava, red in color and charming,
he should perform the mantra-enclosing from the thumb through the little finger, with 'phaṭ.'
At the end he should first perform the placement on the two palms.
He should place them in order on heart, head, topknot, armor, and eyes.
Then, remembering the eight syllables of the root mantra and also oṃ,
he should place them in order on the face, back, belly, arms, private parts, feet, shanks, and hips.
He should place the eight syllables, remembering also the oṃ-syllable.

children.text: ebhiḥ prakārairatiśuddhadehaḥ pūjāṃ sadaivārhati nānyathā hi
children.translated_text: By these methods, a person whose body is exceedingly purified is always fit for worship; otherwise, indeed, he is not.

children.text: śarīraśuddhiṃ manaso niveśaṃ bhūtaprasāraṃ kurute nṛṇāṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: This brings about bodily purification, fixing of the mind, and extension of the elements for human beings.
The Blessed Lord said:
Then, in the arghya vessel, he should recite that mantra eightfold.
With it he should purify the waters, the flowers, his own maṇḍala, and then the seat,
and thereafter all the implements of worship equally.

children.text: oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ iti mantreṇa śabdaprāṃśuvivarjitam ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra 'oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ,' devoid of audible and raised sound,

children.text: dvārapālaṃ tato devyā āsanāni ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: he should then worship the door-guard and the seats of the Goddess.
The gatekeepers are <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and <s>Gaṇeśa</s>;
they should be worshipped in order beginning with the north, and the seats in the middle.
One should worship those beginning with <s>Ādhāraśakti</s> and ending with <s>Hemādri</s>,
well known in all tantras and manuals of worship, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
Together with the guardians of the ten directions, and also <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the others,
one should worship them at the sides, in the corners beginning with the fire-corner of the maṇḍala.
The maṇḍalas of the sun, fire, moon, and winds, and the lotus,

children.text: rajastathā tamaḥ sattvaṃ yogapīṭhaṃ guroḥ padam ||
children.translated_text: then <s>rajas</s>, <s>tamas</s>, and <s>sattva</s>, the yogic seat, and the place of the guru,
those beginning with <s>Sāra</s> and ending with <s>Bhadrapīṭha</s>, together with their limbs and subsidiary limbs, should be worshipped.
Likewise the cosmic egg, the golden egg, and <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
the seven continents with the oceans, the golden island with its pavilion,
the jewel-lotus with its couch, and also the jeweled pillar.
In the very middle of the maṇḍala one must worship the five-faced one.

children.text: hrīṃ mantreṇa tataḥ kūrmapṛṣṭhaṃ pāṇyornibadhya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the mantra <s>hrīṃ</s>, having bound the tortoise-back with the hands,
one should meditate as before on the Goddess, having reached the excellent seat.
In the middle of the heart one should imagine the golden island furnished with a couch.
Then, as if seeing the Goddess, one should remember her with concentrated mind.
Having made her present in the heart, with mental offerings
one should worship the auspicious one abiding in the heart with the sixteen kinds of service.

children.text: tatastu vāyubījena dakṣiṇe ca puṭena ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, by means of the wind-syllable and through the right nostril,

children.text: nāsikāyā viniḥsārya krīṃ mantreṇa ca bhairava
children.translated_text: one should bring her out from the nose with the mantra <s>krīṃ</s>, O <s>Bhairava</s>,
and establish her in the middle of the lotus; one should not separate that hand from it.
If the hand is separated from that flower, O <s>Bhairava</s>,
the Goddess is worshipped by the <s>Gandharvas</s>, but the worshippers do not obtain the fruit.

children.text: āvāhanaṃ tataḥ kuryād gāyatryā śirasā saha
children.translated_text: Then one should perform the invocation with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> along with its head.
We know <s>Mahāmāyā</s>; we meditate on you who are called <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.

children.text: etaduktvā tataḥ paścād dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt
children.translated_text: Having said this, afterwards: May that one impel our thoughts.

children.text: snānīyaṃ devi te tubhyam oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ nama ityataḥ ||
children.translated_text: O Goddess, this bathing water is for you: <s>oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ</s>.
Then one should give bathing water to the Goddess, furnished with the proper marks.
After that, with the root mantra, one should offer sandal-paste and flowers together with a lamp,

children.text: dhūpādikaṃ pradadyāt tu modakaṃ pāyasaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: and should present incense and the rest, and also <s>modaka</s> cakes and milk-rice,
sugar, molasses, curds, milk, ghee, and various kinds of fruits,
red flowers, garlands of flowers, gold, silver, and so on.
As excellent food offering for the Goddess: <s>lāṅgala</s>, <s>modaka</s>, and sugar,
the fruits called <s>śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>karatāmra</s>, and <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>,
also the fruit of <s>harītakī</s>, and <s>nāgaraṅga</s> and <s>kamelaka</s>,
and whatever substance is dear to children, such as <s>kaseruka</s>, lotus-fiber, and the like,

children.text: toyaṃ ca nārikelasya devyai deyaṃ prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and coconut water should be carefully given to the Goddess.

children.text: raktaṃ kauśeyavastraṃ ca deyaṃ nīlaṃ kadāpi na
children.translated_text: Red silk cloth should be given; blue should never be given.

children.text: devyāḥ priyāṇi puṣpāṇi bakulaṃ keśaraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: The flowers dear to the Goddess are <s>bakula</s> and <s>keśara</s>,
<s>māghya</s>, water-lilies, <s>vajra</s> flowers, oleander, and <s>kuruṇṭaka</s>,
arka flowers, śālmalaka, and very tender shoots of dūrvā grass,
sprays of kuśa, darbha grass, and bandhūka and lotus flowers,
mālūra leaves and flowers, and the red-leaved trisandhyā plant.
These flowers are dear to <s>Ambikā</s>, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
Bandhūka, bakula, māghya, bilva leaves, and saṃdhyaka
are best among all flowers; among substances, milk-rice and <s>modaka</s> cakes are best.
A garland of bandhūka flowers, or of bakula, should be offered to <s>Śivā</s>.
Whoever gives thousands of karavīra or māghya flowers

children.text: sa kāmānprāpya cābhīṣṭān mama loke pramodate ||
children.translated_text: obtains the desired objects and delights in my world.
Cool sandalwood, together with <s>kālīyaka</s>,
should be carefully given to the Goddess as the chief unguent.
Camphor, saffron, <s>kūrca</s>, fragrant musk,
and <s>kālīyaka</s> are, among perfumes, supremely pleasing to the Goddess.
<s>Yakṣadhūpa</s>, <s>pratīvāha</s>, ball-incense together with pellets,
aguru and sindhuvāra are considered incenses that give pleasure.
Among body colorings, vermilion is supremely pleasing to the Goddess.
Fragrant rice-food, accompanied by honey and meat,

children.text: apūpaṃ pāyasaṃ kṣīram annaṃ devyāḥ praśasyate
children.translated_text: cakes, milk-rice, milk, and cooked rice are praised for the Goddess.
Jewel-water with camphor, <s>piṇḍītaka</s> and <s>kumāraka</s>,
yellow pigment and <s>puṣpaka</s> are declared to be the Goddess's bathing substances.
Among lamps, a ghee-lamp is proclaimed to be excellent.
One should offer three handfuls of flowers, beautiful, with the root mantra.
Having given all the services, one should worship these goddesses in the middle:
<s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, <s>Guptadurgā</s>, <s>Vindhyakandaravāsinī</s>,
<s>Koṭeśvarī</s>, the one called <s>Dīrghikā</s>, <s>Prakaṭī</s>, and <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s>,
<s>Ākāśagaṅgā</s>, <s>Kāmākhyā</s>, and the one who dwells at <s>Dikkara</s>,

children.text: mātaṅgīṃ lalitāṃ durgāṃ bhairavīṃ siddhidāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mātaṅgī</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Bhairavī</s>, and <s>Siddhidā</s>,
<s>Balapramathinī</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Caṇḍogrā</s>, and <s>Caṇḍanāyikā</s>,

children.text: ugrāṃ bhīmāṃ śivāṃ śāntāṃ jayantīṃ kālikāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ugrā</s>, <s>Bhīmā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Śāntā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, and <s>Kālikā</s>,

children.text: maṅgalāṃ bhadrakālīṃ ca śivāṃ dhātrīṃ kapālinīm
children.translated_text: <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Dhātrī</s>, and <s>Kapālinī</s>,
<s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>, <s>Aparṇā</s>, and <s>Pañcapuṣkariṇī</s>,
<s>Damanī</s>, subduer of all beings, the one who rouses the mind,
<s>Damanī</s>, subduer of all beings, and the sixty-four yoginīs.

children.text: etāḥ sampūjya madhye tu mantreṇāṅgāni pūjayet
children.translated_text: Having fully worshipped these in the middle, one should worship the limbs with the mantra:
the heart, head, topknot, armor, eyes, arms, and feet.
With the three initial syllables of the root mantra and the like, one should perform the worship of the first limbs.
Afterwards, in the worship of the full group of limbs, one should increase the mantras one by one.

children.text: siddhasūtraṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca khaḍgamantreṇa pūjayet
children.translated_text: One should worship the siddha-thread and the sword with the sword-mantra.
Then, in the middle of the eight-petalled lotus, one should worship the eight Yoginīs.
One should worship <s>Śailaputrī</s>, <s>Caṇḍaghaṇṭā</s>, and <s>Skandamātā</s>,
and <s>Kālarātrī</s> in the four directions beginning with the east.
Then one should worship <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍī</s>, and the auspicious <s>Kātyāyanī</s>,
and <s>Mahāgaurī</s>, in the southeast corner and in the quarters beginning with the southwest.
With the root mantra, and with the words 'O <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, forgive me,' eightfold,

children.text: pūjayet padmamadhye tu balidānaṃ tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: one should worship in the middle of the lotus. After that comes the giving of bali.

children.text: evaṃ yadā kalpavidhānamānaiḥ sampūjyate bhairava kāmadevī
children.translated_text: When, O <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Kāmadevī</s> is worshipped in this way according to the measures prescribed by the ritual rule,

children.text: tadā svayaṃ maṇḍalametya deyaṃ gṛhṇāti kāmaṃ ca dadāti samyak ||
children.translated_text: then she herself comes to the maṇḍala, accepts what is to be given, and rightly grants the desired object.
The Blessed Lord said:
After that one should perform the giving of bali, which delights the goddess.
With sweet cakes one should satisfy the elephant-faced one, and with oblation one should satisfy the Sun.
With music, dance, and song, and with observances, one should satisfy <s>Śaṃkara</s> and <s>Hari</s>.
The practitioner should always satisfy <s>Caṇḍikā</s> by the giving of bali.
Birds, tortoises, crocodiles, goats, and boars,

children.text: mahiṣo godhikā śoṣā tathā navavidhā mṛgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the buffalo, the godhikā lizard, śoṣas, and the nine kinds of deer,
the cāmara, the black antelope, the hare, and also the lion,
fish, and the blood of one's own body: these are the eight great kinds of bali.
And when these are not available, at some time a horse and an elephant,
goats, śarabhas, and a human being are used in due order.
These offerings are proclaimed as bali and mahābali.
Having bathed the bali there, with flowers, sandal paste, and incense,
the practitioner should worship the goddess again and again with the bali mantras.
Having faced north, and having the bali face east,
the practitioner should look at it and afterwards utter this mantra:
'You are excellent, present here in the form of bali through my good fortune.
Therefore I bow to you, who have every form and who have the form of strength.
Through the gift that gives pleasure to <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, you are the remover of danger for the giver.
O bali, again and again homage to you, who have the form of the Vaiṣṇavī bali.
Animals were created by <s>Svayambhū</s> himself for the sake of sacrifice.
Therefore I kill you today; hence killing in sacrifice is not killing.'

children.text: oṃ aiṃ hīṃ śrīṃ iti mantreṇa taṃ baliṃ kāmarūpiṇam ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra 'oṃ aiṃ hīṃ śrīṃ,' one should imagine that bali as taking any desired form.

children.text: cintayitvā nyasetpuṣpaṃ mūrdhni tasya ca bhairava
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Bhairava</s>, one should place a flower on its head.
Then, directing it to the goddess and directing it to one's own desire,
after sprinkling the bali, one should worship the sword.
'You are the tongue of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, accomplishing the world of the gods.'

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ iti mantreṇa dhyātvā khaḍgaṃ prapūjayet
children.translated_text: With the mantra 'aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ,' having meditated on the sword, one should worship it.
One should meditate on it as black, as <s>Pinākapāṇi</s>, and as having the form of <s>Kālarātrī</s>,
fierce, with mouth and eyes red, anointed with red garlands and unguents,
wearing red garments, single, holding a noose in the hand, accompanied by its retinue,
drinking blood and eating a heap of raw flesh.
'You are the sword, the slaughterer, the blade, sharp-edged and hard to approach.
O <s>Dharmapāla</s>, <s>Śrīgarva</s>, and <s>Vijaya</s>, homage to you.'

children.text: pūjayitvā tataḥ khaḍgam oṃ āṃ hrīṃ phaḍitimantrakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having then worshipped the sword with the mantras 'oṃ āṃ hrīṃ phaṭ,'
one should take up the spotless sword and cut the excellent bali.
Then one should carefully prepare the blood of the bali offerings
with water, salt, good fruits, honey, fragrances, and flowers.

children.text: oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kauśikīti rudhiraṃ dāpayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: With 'oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kauśikī,' one should say, 'I give this blood to you.'
One should place the blood in the proper place, and the head together with a lamp.

children.text: evaṃ dattvā baliṃ pūrṇaṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti sādhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having given a complete bali in this way, the practitioner obtains the fruit.
If it is deficient, it becomes rooted in deficiency; if it is done contrary to rule, it is fruitless.

children.text: balidāne tu durgāyā anyatrāpi vidhiḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: In the giving of bali to <s>Durgā</s>, and elsewhere too, this rule is always
to be applied by good people; likewise for <s>Vetāla</s> and <s>Bhairava</s>.
Afterwards one should begin the recitation, having undertaken meditation as before.
Taking the rosary in the hand, one should contemplate <s>Śivā</s> with the mind.

children.text: cintayitvā guruṃ mūrdhni yathā varṇādikaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having contemplated the guru on the head, in whatever manner the letters and other elements are,

children.text: mantraṃ ca kaṇṭhato dhyātvā sitavarṇaṃ hiraṇmayam
children.translated_text: and having meditated on the mantra in the throat, white in color and golden,
and on <s>Mahāmāyā</s> in the heart, and oneself at the guru's feet,
one should then declare the unity of the guru, the mantra, and oneself,
and also, having meditated on the oneness of the goddess, then by the path of the suṣumnā,
one should make the six-cakra, which is one in essential reality, descend or be attained.
Having carefully meditated for a moment on <s>Mahāmāyā</s> even in the six-cakra,
one should suspend or extend, by the root alone, the cakra of the sixteen beginning with va.
While contemplating the goddess, who stands in the cakra of the initial sixteen and brings joy to practitioners,
the practitioner should begin the act of recitation.
Above the eyebrows is said to be the end-point of the three nāḍīs.
That end-point is the place of the three paths, a hexagon four finger-breadths in size.
It is red in color and is called the ājñā-cakra by those who know yoga.

children.text: kaṇṭhe trayāṇāṃ nāḍīnāṃ veṣṭanaṃ vidyate nṛṇām
children.translated_text: In the throat of human beings there is an encircling of the three nāḍīs,
of the suṣumnā, iḍā, and piṅgalā; that hexagon is six finger-breadths in size.

children.text: tat ṣaṭcakramiti proktaṃ śuklaṃ kaṇṭhasya madhyagam
children.translated_text: That is called the six-cakra, white, situated in the middle of the throat.
Then, in the heart, there is the unity of the three nāḍīs.
That place is sixteen-spoked, measuring seven finger-breadths.
Employed by those who know yoga, it has the first sixteen-cakra arrangement.
Since, among meditations, mantras, contemplation, and japa,

children.text: yasmād ādyaṃ tu hṛdayaṃ tasmādādīti gadyate ||
children.translated_text: the heart is first, therefore it is called the beginning.
At the beginning of japa one should worship the rosary, carefully sprinkling it with water,
after placing it inside the mandala, or else holding it in the left hand.
"Oṃ, O rosary, rosary, great <s>māyā</s>, embodiment of all powers,
the four aims of life are deposited in you; therefore become the giver of accomplishment to me."

children.text: pūjayitvā tato mālāṃ gṛhṇīyād dakṣiṇe kare
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the rosary, one should then take it in the right hand,
at the middle part of the middle finger, avoiding the index finger.
With the ring finger and little finger joined at their bent part,
having placed the rosary there, one should move what is on it with the tip of the thumb.
Taking each bead one by one, one should perform japa by half, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
At each turn one should recite the mantra and move the lips softly.
The bead of the rosary that has been recited over should not touch another.
Nor, O <s>Bhairava</s>, should it be touched with the thumb used for the previous recitation.

children.text: pūrvabījaṃ japan yastu parabījaṃ ca saṃspṛśet
children.translated_text: Whoever, while reciting over the previous bead, touches the next bead
with his thumb, for him that japa becomes fruitless.
Holding the rosary near one's own heart with the right hand,

children.text: devīṃ vicintayan japyaṃ kuryād vāmena na spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: one should do the japa while contemplating the goddess; one should not touch it with the left hand.
With crystal, <s>indrākṣa</s>, rudrākṣa, beads produced from putrañjīva,
with gold beads, or properly with coral, or with lotus seeds,
a rosary of beads should be made, supremely pleasing to the goddess.
One should always recite in a low murmur, or with a knot of kuśa grass, or by the hand.
Among all rosary beads, rudrākṣa is especially dear to me.
Because it pleases <s>Rudra</s>, therefore the rudrākṣa is delightful.
Alternatively, one should make it of coral, with twenty-eight beads,
or with fifty-five, neither fewer nor more.
If one recites with rudrākṣas, or likewise with <s>indrākṣas</s> or crystals,

children.text: nānyaṃ madhye prayoktavyaṃ putrañjīvādikaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: nothing else, such as putrañjīva and the like, should be inserted among them.
But if anything else is used in the rosary for the act of japa,

children.text: tasya kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca dadāti na priyaṃkarī ||
children.translated_text: the beloved goddess does not grant him either desire or liberation.
It then comes into a mixed state, like that of sinful cāṇḍālas.
In another birth he is born learned in the Veda and the Vedāṅgas.
One meru bead should be placed there, larger than all the others.
The first should be large; after that, each should be smaller and still smaller.

children.text: vinyaset kramatas tasmāt sarpākārā hi sā yataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore one should arrange them in order, since it has the form of a serpent.
One should make it furnished with a <s>brahmagranthi</s> (Brahmā-knot), each bead remaining in its place.
Or else it may be without knots, fitted with a firm cord,
with a double turn, then through the middle, and with a half-turn at the end-region.
A knot turning clockwise is known as a <s>brahmagranthi</s>.
One should string the rosary oneself; a man without mantra should not string it.

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ sūtraṃ niyuñjīta jape truṭyati no yathā
children.translated_text: One should attach a strong thread, so that it does not break during japa,

children.text: yathā hastānna cyaveta japataḥ srak tamācaret ||
children.translated_text: and should make the garland so that it does not slip from the hand while one is reciting.
If it falls from the hand there will be an obstacle; if it breaks, death will occur.

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ kurute mālāṃ japaṃ ca japakovidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, the expert in japa who makes a rosary and performs japa

children.text: sa prāpnotīpsitaṃ kāmaṃ hīne syāttu viparyayaḥ
children.translated_text: obtains the desired aim he longs for; if it is deficient, the opposite occurs.
Elsewhere too one should recite with a rosary the japa pleasing to the deity.
Such a practitioner should do it, and never otherwise.
According to one's ability, one should perform japa carefully by number.

children.text: asaṃkhyātaṃ ca yajjaptaṃ tasya tanniṣphalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Whatever is recited without counting becomes fruitless.

children.text: japtvā mālāṃ śirodeśe prāṃśusthāne'tha vā nyaset ||
children.translated_text: After reciting, one should place the rosary on the region of the head or in a high place.

children.text: stutipāṭhaṃ tataḥ kuryādiṣṭaṃ kāmaṃ nivedya ca
children.translated_text: Then one should recite the praise, after stating the desired object.
The praise too is a great mantra, the means for all rites.
I shall tell it to you two, O greatly fortunate ones, as bestowing all accomplishments.
"O auspicious one among all that is auspicious, O <s>Śivā</s>, accomplisher of every aim,

children.text: śaraṇye tryambake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te
children.translated_text: O refuge, three-eyed <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, homage to you."
Having repeated this praise seven times, the practitioner

children.text: pañcapraṇāmān kṛtvātha aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ itimantrakaiḥ
children.translated_text: should then make five prostrations with the mantras "aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ."
In front of others, or more than that, he may do so as he wishes.
After that, having shown the yonimudrā, he should dismiss the deity.
Stretching out both hands and making an upturned añjali,
he should place the two tips of the thumbs on the two tips of the little fingers.
He should set the little finger of the left hand forward on the ring finger,
and the little finger of the right hand on the right ring finger.

children.text: anāmikāyāḥ pṛṣṭhe tu madhyame dve niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: On the backs of the ring fingers he should place the two middle fingers.
He should join the two index fingers to the tips of the little fingers with their own tips.
This is called the yonimudrā and is regarded as pleasing to the goddess.

children.text: trivāraṃ darśayet tāṃ tu mūlamantreṇa sādhakaḥ
children.translated_text: The practitioner should show it three times with the root mantra.

children.text: tāṃ mudrāṃ śirasi nyasya maṇḍalaṃ vinyaset tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Placing that mudrā on his head, he should then arrange the mandala.
In the northeast, with the front of the hand, without gate or lotus,

children.text: tatra natvā raktacaṇḍāṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ mantreṇa sādhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the practitioner should bow to <s>Raktacaṇḍā</s> with the mantra "hrīṃ śrīṃ."

children.text: raktacaṇḍāyai nama iti nirmālyaṃ tatra nikṣipet
children.translated_text: Saying "homage to <s>Raktacaṇḍā</s>," he should deposit the discarded offerings there.

children.text: udake tarumūle vā nirmālyaṃ tatra saṃtyajet ||
children.translated_text: He should leave the discarded offerings there in water or at the root of a tree.

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ pūjayed devīṃ vidhānena śivāṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who worships the goddess <s>Śivā</s> in this way according to the rule
quickly obtains all the desires that are in his mind.
After first reciting a half-lakh of japa, the practitioner
should perform the preliminary observance in particular, with presentations of various food offerings.
Having made the fire-pit in the form of a maṇḍala, and having fasted on the eighth lunar day,
on the ninth day of the bright fortnight a man, with the five powders,
should make the maṇḍala as before, in the presence of his guru and parents,
and, by this very procedure, should worship <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
With bilva leaves as well, three hundred and eight in number,
he should perform the homa with sesame seeds and should recite three thousand times.

children.text: naivedyaṃ gandhapuṣpe ca vastraṃ dadyācca yatpriyam
children.translated_text: He should give food offering, fragrance and flowers, clothing, and whatever is dear to her,
and he should also give to her what was previously stated, and rice pudding as well.
At the end of the worship, three offerings of that same kind should be given,
together with vermilion, gold, jewels, and whatever is an ornament of women.
According to his ability he should present flowers and garlands in abundance.
On the ninth day he should give to the goddess a complete bali, a great śaktu offering with cooked rice,

children.text: devyai navamyāṃ sampūrṇaṃ baliṃ dadyād ghṛtādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: together with preparations from cow products and with ghee and the like.

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ gurave dadyātsuvarṇaṃ gāṃ tathā tilam ||
children.translated_text: He should give a fee to the guru: gold, a cow, and sesame seeds.
One should avoid, in matters of mantra, a guru who is cursed, childless, blameworthy, a cheat,
deficient in rites, ignorant of the kalpa, a dwarf, or a reviler of gurus,
and one who is always filled with envy.
The guru is the root of the mantra; when the root is pure, what arises from it
becomes fruitful. Therefore one should carefully examine the mantra.
Through deceit, anger, delusion, or evil intention, one should not take a mantra from the guru's mouth

children.text: kalpeṣu dṛṣṭvā vā mantraṃ gṛhṇīyācchadmanātha vā
children.translated_text: after seeing it in the kalpas, nor by trickery.
Because of the sin of stealing a mantra, that man, in the <s>Tāmisra</s> hell,
dwells for three manvantaras and is then born in sinful wombs.

children.text: śaṭhe krūre ca mūrkhe ca chadmakāriṇyabhaktike ||
children.translated_text: One should not give a mantra, polluted like good seed cast in a wilderness,

children.text: mantraṃ na dūṣite dadyāt subījaṃ vipine tathā
children.translated_text: to one who is deceitful, cruel, foolish, fraudulent, or without devotion.
With one lakh recitations, preceded by the preliminary observance, he should accomplish his desire,
since the destruction of sin occurs through the rite of preliminary observance.
O best of men, with two lakhs of japa of the mantra,
daily at the three junctions of the day and with the aggregate of seed syllables,
the practitioner becomes a poet, eloquent, learned, and famous.
O best of practitioners, practitioner, now hear the place for worship.

children.text: yatra yatra naraḥ pūjāṃ nirjane kurute ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wherever a man performs worship in a solitary place,

children.text: tasyādatte svayaṃ devī patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: the goddess herself accepts from him leaf, flower, fruit, and water.

children.text: śilā praśastā pūjāyāṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ nirjanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: A stone is praised for worship, and likewise a solitary altar-ground.
Whispered japa is declared the best for all.
One who is impure should never worship <s>Mahāmāyā</s>.
But the man who is filled with great devotion should certainly remember the mantra.

children.text: dantarakte samutpanne smaraṇaṃ ca na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: When blood has arisen from the teeth, there is no remembrance;
for with regard to all mantras, from remembrance then one goes to hell.

children.text: jānūrdhve kṣataje jāte nityaṃ karma na cācaret ||
children.translated_text: When blood appears above the knees, one should not perform the regular rite.

children.text: naimittikaṃ ca tadadhaḥ sravadrakto na cācaret
children.translated_text: If blood is flowing below that, one should not perform the occasional rite either.
When impurity from birth occurs, during shaving, during sexual intercourse,
during belching smoke, and after vomiting, one should abandon the regular rites.

children.text: dravye bhukte tvajīrṇe ca na vai bhuktvā ca kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: When food has been eaten and is undigested, or after having eaten anything at all,

children.text: karma kuryānnaro nityaṃ sūtake mṛtake tathā
children.translated_text: a man should perform no regular rite, and likewise during impurity from birth or death.

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ bheṣajatvena kalpitam ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten leaf, flower, betel, or what has been prepared as medicine,

children.text: kaṇādipippalyantaṃ ca phalaṃ bhuktvā na cācaret
children.translated_text: and fruit down to grains and long pepper, one should not perform the rite.
O best of men, even after taking water, apart from food or medicine,
the regular observance, together with occasional rites, should always cease.
Having intentionally touched with the hand a leech, a hidden-footed creature,
worms, earthworms, and the like, one should abandon the regular rites.
In particular, a man whose father has died should not perform the worship of <s>Śivā</s>,
even mentally, until a full year has passed.
On the death of a great guru, one should perform no optional rite at all.

children.text: ārtvijyaṃ brahmayajñaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ devayajaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Officiating as a priest, brahmayajña, śrāddha, and whatever is sacrifice to the gods,

children.text: gurumākṣipya vipraṃ ca prahṛtyaiva ca pāṇinā ||
children.translated_text: after insulting a guru or striking a Brahmin with the hand,
one should not perform the regular rites, and also at emission of semen, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
One should not use a broken seat or vessel for arghya.
One should not worship in a barren place, in a place full of worms, or even in an unclean place.
Having taken a low seat, being pure and with a controlled mind,
one should worship the goddess <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, or another deity, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
Among the divisions of the directions, the northern direction, belonging to <s>Kubera</s>, gives pleasure to <s>Śivā</s>.
Therefore, seated facing that direction, one should always worship <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
A flower mixed with worms, withered, broken, or fallen on the ground,
with hair in it, or shaken by mice, one should carefully avoid.

children.text: yācitaṃ parakīyaṃ ca tathā paryuṣitaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: What has been begged, belongs to another, or is stale,
what has been cast off by an outcaste or touched by the foot, one should carefully avoid.

children.text: idaṃ śivāyāḥ paramaṃ manoharaṃ karoti yo'nena tadīyapūjanam
children.translated_text: Whoever performs the worship of <s>Śivā</s> with this supreme and delightful rite

children.text: sa vāñchitārthaṃ samavāpya caṇḍikāgṛhaṃ prayātā nacireṇa bhairava ||
children.translated_text: obtains the desired object and before long goes to the abode of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:
Hear the kavaca of this mantra, O <s>Vetālabhairava</s>,
especially of <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, known as the <s>Vaiṣṇavī Tantra</s>.
There the first syllable of the mantra bears the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s>;
the second letter is <s>Brahmā</s> himself, and the third is <s>Candraśekhara</s>.
The fourth is <s>Gajavaktra</s>, and the fifth is <s>Divākara</s>.
The syllable pa is <s>Śakti</s> herself; she is <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, consisting of the world.
The syllable ya is <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>; the remaining syllable is <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
For the first syllable, the yoginī is proclaimed to be <s>Śailaputrī</s>.

children.text: dvitīyasya tu varṇasya caṇḍikā yoginī matā
children.translated_text: For the second syllable, the yoginī is regarded as <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
For the third it is <s>Candraghaṇṭā</s>, and for the one after that <s>Kuṣmāṇḍī</s>.
For the syllable ta it is <s>Skandamātā</s>; behold, <s>Kātyāyanī</s> herself
is established as the seventh, while <s>Kālarātrī</s> is <s>Mahādevī</s>.
First comes the kavaca of the syllables, and likewise the kavaca of the yoginīs;
then the kavaca of the hosts of gods, and likewise the kavaca of the goddess in the directions.
After that comes the kavaca of the sides, and of the indeclinable ending in the second case;

children.text: kavacaṃ tu tataḥ paścāt ṣaḍvarṇaṃ kavacaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: then the kavaca, and afterwards the six-syllabled kavaca as well.
And there is the unbreakable kavaca, wholly devoted to protection everywhere.
The best of men who knows these eight kavacas
is I myself, O <s>Mahādevī</s>, bearing the form of the goddess and endowed with power.
Of this Vaiṣṇavī-tantra kavaca, <s>Nārada</s> is the seer and the meter is anuṣṭubh.
<s>Kātyāyanī</s> is the deity; its application is for accomplishing every desired aim.

children.text: aḥ pātu pūrvakāṣṭhāyāmāgneyyāṃ pātu kaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: May aḥ protect me in the eastern quarter; may ka always protect me in the southeast.

children.text: pātu co yamakāṣṭhāyāṃ do nairṛtyāṃ ca sarvadā
children.translated_text: May o protect me in the quarter of <s>Yama</s>, and may do always protect me in the southwest.

children.text: māṃ pātu to'sau pāścātye śaktir vāyavyadiggatā ||
children.translated_text: May to protect me in the west; <s>Śakti</s> is stationed in the northwest direction.
May ya protect me in the north, and may ya likewise guard me in the northeast.

children.text: mūrdhni rakṣatu māṃ so'sau bāhau māṃ dakṣiṇe tu kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May that one protect me on the head; may ka protect me on the right arm.

children.text: māṃ vāmabāhau caḥ pātu hṛdi ṭo māṃ sadāvatu
children.translated_text: May ca protect me on the left arm; may ṭo always guard me in the heart.

children.text: taḥ pātu kaṇṭhadeśe māṃ kaṭyoḥ śaktistathāvatu ||
children.translated_text: May ta protect me in the region of the throat; may <s>Śakti</s> likewise guard my hips.

children.text: yaḥ pātu dakṣiṇe pāde ṣo māṃ vāmapāde tathā
children.translated_text: May ya protect my right foot, and may ṣo likewise protect my left foot.
May <s>Śailaputrī</s> protect me in the east, and may <s>Caṇḍikā</s> protect me in the southeast.
May <s>Candraghaṇṭā</s>, who increases fear of <s>Yama</s>, protect me in the south.

children.text: nairṛtye tvatha kūṣmāṇḍī pātu māṃ jagatāṃ prasūḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in the southwest may <s>Kūṣmāṇḍī</s>, mother of the worlds, protect me.

children.text: skandamātā paścimāyāṃ māṃ rakṣatu sadaiva hi
children.translated_text: May <s>Skandamātā</s> always protect me in the west.

children.text: kātyāyanī māṃ vāyavye pātu lokeśvarī sadā ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, mistress of the world, always protect me in the northwest.

children.text: kālarātrī tu kauberyāṃ sadā rakṣatu māṃ svayam
children.translated_text: May <s>Kālarātrī</s> herself always protect me in the northern quarter of <s>Kubera</s>.
And may <s>Mahāgaurī</s>, the purifier, constantly protect me in the northeast.
May eternal <s>Vāsudeva</s> always protect me in the two eyes.

children.text: brahmā māṃ pātu vadane padmayonir ayonijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born, unborn one, protect me in the face.
May <s>Candraśekhara</s> always protect me in the region of the nose.
May <s>Gajavaktra</s>, son of <s>Hara</s>, always protect the pair of breasts.
May <s>Divākara</s> always protect me in the left and right hands.

children.text: mahāmāyā svayaṃ nābhau māṃ pātu parameśvarī ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Mahāmāyā</s> herself, the supreme lady, protect me at the navel.
May <s>Mahālakṣmī</s> protect me in the genitals, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> at the knees.
May <s>Mahāmāyā</s> always protect me in the front.
And in the southeast may <s>Agnijvālā</s>, bearer of the excellent sword, always protect me.

children.text: rudrāṇī pātu māṃ yāmyāṃ nairṛtyāṃ caṇḍanāyikā ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Rudrāṇī</s> protect me in the south, and <s>Caṇḍanāyikā</s> in the southwest.
May <s>Ugracaṇḍā</s>, the great mistress, always protect me in the west.
May <s>Pracaṇḍā</s> protect me in the northwest, and the fierce-formed one in <s>Kubera</s>'s quarter.

children.text: īśvarī ca tathaiśānyāṃ pātu nityaṃ sanātanī
children.translated_text: And may <s>Īśvarī</s>, the eternal one, likewise always protect me in the northeast.
May <s>Mahāmāyā</s> protect above; may <s>Parameśvarī</s> protect below.

children.text: agrataḥ pātu māmugrā pṛṣṭhato vaiṣṇavī tathā
children.translated_text: May <s>Ugrā</s> protect me in front, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> behind.

children.text: brahmāṇī dakṣiṇe pārśve nityaṃ rakṣatu śobhanā ||
children.translated_text: May beautiful <s>Brahmāṇī</s> always protect my right side.
May <s>Māheśvarī</s>, whose emblem is the bull, always protect my left side.

children.text: kaumārī parvate pātu vārāhī salile ca mām ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Kaumārī</s> protect me on a mountain, and <s>Vārāhī</s> in water.

children.text: nārasiṃhī daṃṣṭribhaye pātu māṃ vipineṣu ca
children.translated_text: May <s>Nārasiṃhī</s> protect me from the fear of fanged beings and in forests.

children.text: aindrī māṃ pātu cākāśe tathā sarvajale sthale ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Aindrī</s> protect me in the sky, and likewise in every water and on land.

children.text: setuḥ sarvāṅgulīḥ pātu devādiḥ pātu karṇayoḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Setu</s> protect all my fingers; may the beginning of the deity protect my two ears.
May the end of the deity protect my chin, and the fifth <s>Śakti</s> protect my sides.

children.text: hā pātu māṃ tathaivorvormāyā rakṣatu jaṅghayoḥ
children.translated_text: May hā protect me likewise in the thighs; may <s>Māyā</s> protect the shanks.
May ya always protect all the senses and the pores of the hair.

children.text: tvaci māṃ vai sadā pātu māṃ śambhuḥ pātu sarvadā
children.translated_text: May it always protect me in the skin; may <s>Śambhu</s> always protect me.

children.text: nakhadantakaroṣṭhapādau rāṃ māṃ pātu sadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: May rāṃ always protect my nails, teeth, hands, lips, and feet.

children.text: devādiḥ pātu māṃ vastau devāntaḥ stanakakṣayoḥ
children.translated_text: May the beginning of the deity protect me in the bladder; may the end of the deity protect the breasts and armpits.

children.text: etadādau tu yaḥ seturbāhye māṃ pātu dehataḥ ||
children.translated_text: May the bridge that stands at the beginning of this protect me externally from the body.
In the command cakra, in the suṣumṇā, in the six cakras, in the heart, and in the joints,
and in the first sixteen-petaled cakra, and in the space of the forehead,

children.text: vaiṣṇavī tantramantro māṃ nityaṃ rakṣaṃśca tiṣṭhatu
children.translated_text: may the Vaiṣṇavī tantra-mantra remain always protecting me.
In all the channels of the ears, in the side, armpits, and topknot,
in the blood, sinews, and marrow, in the brains and in the joints,
may the second eight-syllabled mantra protect me as a kavaca on every side.
In the semen, wind, navel aperture, and back-joints everywhere,
may this third six-syllabled mantra always protect me.
May <s>Mahāmāyā</s> protect me in the nostril opening, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> in the throat opening.
May <s>Durgā</s>, remover of distress from difficulties, protect me in all the joints.

children.text: śrotrayor hūṃ phaḍityevaṃ nityaṃ rakṣatu kālikā
children.translated_text: May <s>Kālikā</s> always protect the two ears with the formula hūṃ phaṭ.
May the three eye-seed syllables always remain in the eyes for protection.

children.text: oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ nāsikāyāṃ rakṣantī cāstu caṇḍikā
children.translated_text: May <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, protecting with oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ, also be in the nose.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ māṃ sadā tārā jihvāmūle tu tiṣṭhatu ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Tārā</s>, with oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, always remain at the root of my tongue.

children.text: hṛdi tiṣṭhatu me seturjñānaṃ rakṣitum uttamam
children.translated_text: May <s>Setu</s> remain in my heart to protect the highest knowledge.

children.text: oṃ kṣauṃ phaṭ ca mahāmāyā pātu māṃ sarvataḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: And may <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, with oṃ kṣauṃ phaṭ, always protect me everywhere.

children.text: oṃ yuṃ saḥ prāṇān kauśikī māṃ prāṇānrakṣatu rakṣikā
children.translated_text: Oṃ yuṃ saḥ: may <s>Kauśikī</s>, the protectress, protect my life-breaths.

children.text: hrīṃ hūṃ sauṃ bhargadayitā dehaśūnyeṣu pātu mām ||
children.translated_text: Hrīṃ hūṃ sauṃ: may the beloved of <s>Bharga</s> protect me in places empty of bodies.

children.text: oṃ namaḥ sadā śailaputrī sarvān rogān pramṛjyatām
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage always to <s>Śailaputrī</s>; may all diseases be wiped away.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ saḥ spheṃ kṣaḥ phaḍastrāya siṃhavyāghrabhayādraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ saḥ spheṃ kṣaḥ phaṭ, for the missile; may it protect from fear of lions, tigers, and battle.

children.text: śivadūtī pātu nityaṃ hrīṃ sarvāstreṣu tiṣṭhatu
children.translated_text: May <s>Śivadūtī</s> always protect; hrīṃ, may she stand firm against all weapons.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ hīṃ saścaṇḍaghaṇṭā karṇacchidreṣu pātu mām ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ saḥ: may <s>Caṇḍaghaṇṭā</s> protect me in the openings of the ears.

children.text: oṃ krīṃ saḥ kāmeśvarī kāmānabhitiṣṭhatu rakṣatu
children.translated_text: Oṃ krīṃ saḥ: may <s>Kāmeśvarī</s> preside over and protect desires.

children.text: oṃ āṃ hūṃ phaḍugracaṇḍā ripūn vighnān vimardatām ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ āṃ hūṃ phaṭ: may fierce <s>Caṇḍā</s> crush enemies and obstacles.

children.text: oṃ aṃ śūlātpātu nityaṃ vaiṣṇavī jagadīśvarī
children.translated_text: Oṃ aṃ: may <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, mistress of the world, always protect from the spear.

children.text: oṃ kaṃ brahmāṇī pātu cakrāt ca rudrāṇī tu śaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ kaṃ: may <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> protect from the discus, and <s>Rudrāṇī</s> from the spear-power.

children.text: oṃ ṭaṃ kaumārī pātu vajrāttaṃ vārāhī tu kāṇḍataḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ ṭaṃ: may <s>Kaumārī</s> protect from the thunderbolt, and <s>Vārāhī</s> from arrows.

children.text: oṃ paṃ pātu nārasiṃhī māṃ kravyādebhyastathāstrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ paṃ: may <s>Nārasiṃhī</s> protect me from flesh-eating beings and also from missiles.
From every weapon and missile, from devices, and from hostile mantras,

children.text: caṇḍikā māṃ sadā pātu yaṃ saṃ devyai namo namaḥ
children.translated_text: may <s>Caṇḍikā</s> always protect me. Yaṃ saṃ; homage, homage to the goddess.
From betrayers of trust may <s>Aindrī</s> protect me, and may she protect my mind.

children.text: oṃ namo mahāmāyāyai oṃ vaiṣṇavyai namo namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Mahāmāyā</s>; oṃ, homage, homage to <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>.
Protect me from all beings, everywhere, O supreme goddess.

children.text: ādhāre vāyumārge hṛdi kamaladale candravat smerasūrye vastau vahnau samiddhe viśatu varadayā mantramaṣṭākṣaraṃ tat
children.translated_text: In the base, in the path of wind, in the heart, in the lotus-petal, in the smiling sun like the moon, and in the blazing fire in the bladder, may that eight-syllabled mantra enter by the boon-giving goddess.

children.text: yadbrahmā mūrdhni dhatte harir avati gale candracūḍo hṛdisthaṃ taṃ māṃ pātu pradhānaṃ nikhilamatiśayaṃ padmagarbhābhabījam ||
children.translated_text: The seed resembling the lotus-born one, which <s>Brahmā</s> bears on his head, which <s>Hari</s> guards at the throat, and which the moon-crested one holds in the heart, may that chief, complete, unsurpassed seed protect me.

children.text: ādyāḥ śeṣāḥ svaraughair mamayavalavarair asvareṇāpi yuktaiḥ sānusvārāvisargair hariharaviditaṃ yatsahasraṃ ca sāṣṭam
children.translated_text: The initial and final sounds, joined with streams of vowels, with the syllables ma, ya, va, la, and with even the soundless, together with anusvāra and visarga, make the thousand and eight known to <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ setubandhaṃ nivasati satataṃ vaiṣṇavītantramantre tanmāṃ pāyātpavitraṃ paramaparamajaṃ bhūtalavyomabhāge ||
children.translated_text: That pure, supreme, unborn bridge of mantras, dwelling constantly in the Vaiṣṇavī-tantra mantra, may protect me on earth and in the region of the sky.

children.text: aṅgānyaṣṭau tathāṣṭau vasava iha tathaivāṣṭamūrtir dalāni proktānyaṣṭau tathāṣṭau madhumatiracitāḥ siddhayo 'ṣṭau tathaiva
children.translated_text: Here the eight limbs and again eight, the <s>Vasus</s>, the eight forms, and the petals are declared as eight and eight; the accomplishments fashioned by sweet wisdom are likewise eight.

children.text: aṣṭāvaṣṭāṣṭasaṃkhyā jagati ratikalāḥ kṣiprakāṣṭhāṅgayogā mayyaṣṭāvakṣarāṇi kṣaratu na hi gaṇo yaddhṛdo yastvamūṣām ||
children.translated_text: The eight, eight, and eight in number in the world, the arts of delight, the quick units of time, and the bodily yogas: may these eight imperishable syllables flow in me; indeed there is no reckoning of those whose heart is this.
Thus that kavaca has been declared, accomplishing dharma, desire, and wealth.
This is the supreme secret; this accomplishes every aim.
Whoever hears this kavaca even once, as spoken by me,
obtains all desires and, in the next world, the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
And whoever recites this kavaca even once, as spoken by me,

children.text: sa sarvayajñasya phalaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtains the fruit of every sacrifice; there is no doubt about this.
In battles he conquers enemies like a lion conquering elephants.

children.text: dahettṛṇaṃ yathā vahnistathā śatruṃ dahet sadā ||
children.translated_text: As fire burns grass, so he always burns up the enemy.

children.text: nāstrāṇi tasya śastrāṇi śarīre praviśanti vai
children.translated_text: Neither missiles nor weapons enter his body.

children.text: na tasya jāyate vyādhirna ca duḥkhaṃ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: No illness arises for him, nor any suffering at any time.
Pills, collyriums, subterranean rites, foot-ointments, alchemical preparations, and eye-salves,
and all accomplishments such as expulsion rites become favorable to him.
His thought becomes unimpeded by others, like the wind.
He becomes long-lived, enjoying desired pleasures, and wealthy.
Having become restrained on the eighth lunar day, and on the ninth, according to rule,
having worshiped <s>Śivā</s> by the prescribed rite and meditated on <s>Śivā</s> in his mind,

children.text: yo nyaset kavacaṃ dehe tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: if he places the kavaca upon his body, hear the fruit of his merit.
He conquers disease, lives a hundred years, and is always handsome and virtuous.
He is born full of streams of wealth and jewels, and learned.
Fire does not burn that body, nor do waters make it wet.

children.text: na śoṣayati taṃ vāyuḥ kravyāt taṃ na hinasti ca
children.translated_text: Wind does not dry him up, and a flesh-eater does not harm him.

children.text: śastrāṇi nainaṃ chindanti na tāpayati bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Weapons do not cut him, and the sun does not scorch him.

children.text: na tasya jāyate vighno nāsti tasya ca saṃjvaraḥ
children.translated_text: No obstacle arises for him, and he has no fever.
<s>Vetālas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and leaders of hosts
all come under his control, as do the four kinds of spirit-communities.

children.text: nityaṃ paṭhati yo bhaktyā kavacaṃ haranirmitam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever constantly recites with devotion the kavaca fashioned by <s>Hara</s>,
he is myself, <s>Mahādeva</s>, and also <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, the Mother.
Dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation are always in his hand.
He is a giver of boons to another in matters of wealth and is always learned.
Poetic power and truthfulness continually arise in him.
He may utter thousands of verses and becomes one who retains what he has heard.

children.text: likhitaṃ yasya gehe tu kavacaṃ bhairavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: In whose house this written kavaca, established as <s>Bhairava</s>, is kept,

children.text: na tasya durgatiḥ kvāpi jāyate tasya dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: no bad destiny arises for him anywhere, nor any blemish for him.

children.text: grahāśca sarve tuṣyanti vaśaṃ gacchanti bhūmipāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the planets are pleased, and kings come under his control.
In the kingdom where there is one who knows the kavaca, there good policies arise.
The divine bridge, the power-seed: homage to you for the fifth delusion.
With the force of wind, for this goddess, this is the second eight-syllabled mantra.
Then the divine bridge for <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> is remembered as this six-syllabled mantra.

children.text: etad dvayaṃ tu jihvāgre satataṃ yasya vartate
children.translated_text: For the one on whose tongue-tip these two constantly abide,

children.text: tasya devī mahāmāyā kāye tiṣṭhati vai sadā ||
children.translated_text: the goddess <s>Mahāmāyā</s> surely always dwells in his body.
The praṇava is the bridge of mantras; that bridge is remembered as the praṇava.
What has not first been marked with oṃ decays, and afterward it falls apart.
